t: This is Queen's Gate, a street in South Kensington running south from Kensington Gardens to Old Brompton Road, crossing Cromwell Road on the way. Several notable people lived or died along it. A. J. Mundella died here; as education minister under Gladstone he established universal compulsory education in Britain. Sir Thomas Troubridge, who served with distinction in the Crimean War, also died on this street, as did the baronet Sir Herbert Perrott. The army officer Walter Simeon Nathan lived here too.
